items.title: Show the deliverable
items.hypothesis: An inspectable meal plan or appetizing finished meals may communicate the offer more clearly than a lifestyle image.
items.evidence: Observed food-blog offer, not verified conversion evidence. Prepare a plan-only image and a food-only image before testing.

items.title: Reduce mobile scrolling
items.hypothesis: A compact layout may make the offer and email field easier to see together.
items.evidence: A layout treatment is one experimental factor, not proof about each individual spacing change.

items.title: Name the benefit in the button
items.hypothesis: Naming the free meal plan or shopping list may reduce uncertainty at the email submission step.
items.evidence: Concrete deliverables are visible in these offers. Their CVRs are not publicly verified.

items.title: Test the first invitation timing
items.hypothesis: A shorter or longer delay may increase total leads per eligible session.
items.evidence: Vendor observational benchmarks are hypotheses, not causal evidence. Needs variant-specific initial delay and an eligible-session primary metric.

items.title: Give readers more time
items.hypothesis: Waiting longer or not automatically reopening may preserve attention while the reminder tab stays available.
items.evidence: Guardrail-oriented hypothesis. Requires eligible-session conversion as the decision metric before promotion; the first stage evaluates copy tests using popup-viewing sessions.

items.title: Revisit question-first flows
items.hypothesis: One useful question may improve relevance enough to offset the extra step.
items.evidence: Check earlier goal and challenge quizzes first. Any retest needs a documented new context.

items.title: Visual clarity
items.hypothesis: A single typography or contrast change may improve readability without changing the offer.
items.evidence: Do not mix button color, fonts, and background in a single attribute test.

items.title: A different useful deliverable
items.hypothesis: A smaller recipe collection may feel easier to use than a complete plan.
items.evidence: Requires a real deliverable and approval. Never promise an unavailable plan, medical outcome, or invented social proof.
